PlayWright - v1.65.0(435563872)

created: 2026-11-05T17:41:52Z

v1.65.0 (2026-11-05)

🥟 Run tests with Bun

The test runner now runs under Bun. Bun transpiles your TypeScript test files itself, so Playwright does not use Babel or its compilation cache. Pass the --bun flag, because without it bunx playwright test runs on Node.js:

1

bunx --bun playwright test

Our CI runs the test runner tests under Bun 1.4.3 on Linux. Some features work differently under Bun:

  • There is no watch mode. UI mode does not run tests again when files change, and --only-changed does not follow imports.
  • Bun loads modules itself, so --tsconfig and the JSX options in tsconfig.json have no effect, and custom ESM loaders are not supported.
  • Stack traces do not include async frames, and API names do not include the class name: click instead of locator.click. This changes some step locations, step titles and error messages.
  • Console output of a test does not get into the trace and UI mode.

🚨 Reports with only failures

New failures reporter prints failures and successful retries as they occur, followed by a summary, without progress output.

New onlyFailures option of the HTML, JSON and JUnit reporters keeps only tests with unexpected outcomes, flaky tests and interrupted tests:

1

4

// playwright.config.ts
import { defineConfig } from '@playwright/test';

export default defineConfig({
 reporter: [
 ['failures'],
 ['html', { onlyFailures: true }],
 ],
});

🎯 Test runner

  • New built-in -exclusive- test lock runs a test only when no other tests are running. All other tests continue to run in parallel with each other:

    1
2

    test('restart the server', { lock: '-exclusive-' }, async () => {
 // No other test runs while this one is running.
});

  • test.skip(), test.fixme(), test.fail() and test.slow() now accept only a description. It is recorded in the test annotation:

2

 test.skip('Not implemented yet');
});

Pytest - 9.2.0(426006480)

created: 2026-10-27T21:30:34Z

9.2.0 (2026-10-27)

pytest 9.2.0 (2026-10-27)

Removals and backward incompatible breaking changes

  • #14716: -c now raises a usage error for a path that does not exist, is a directory, or is in a format pytest has no loader for. Such paths were previously either ignored or reported as an unhandled FileNotFoundError.

  • #8593: The indirect, ids and scope arguments of Metafunc.parametrize() <pytest.Metafunc.parametrize> – and therefore of @pytest.mark.parametrize <pytest.mark.parametrize ref> – are now keyword-only.

    Passing them positionally was a common source of confusing errors, e.g. parametrize("arg1", "arg2", [(1, 2)]) made the argvalues land in indirect and failed with indirect fixture '(1, 2)' doesn't exist; such mistakes now fail with an understandable TypeError. The type annotations have always declared these arguments as keyword-only.

  • #993: Plugin import failures at startup are now reported and classified instead of escaping as a raw traceback with the accidental exit code 1:

    • a plugin that cannot be found – via -p, pytest_plugins or PYTEST_PLUGINS – exits with pytest.ExitCode USAGE_ERROR (4), like a conftest.py that fails to import;
    • a plugin that is found but raises while importing – including a broken pytest11 entry point or a missing plugin dependency – exits with pytest.ExitCode INTERNAL_ERROR (3), with the traceback preserved.

    pytest.main now returns these codes instead of raising ImportError. Also fixed an IndexError from pytest’s own internals when the plugin raised an exception with no arguments.

Deprecations (removal in next major release)

  • #14742: The private _pytest.python.CallSpec2 name has been renamed to CallSpec. The old CallSpec2 alias remains available for now and will be removed in pytest 10 or 11.

  • #14755: Schedule yield_fixture decorator for removal in pytest 10 or 11.

  • #14774: Similarly to the deprecation of class-scoped fixtures defined as instance methods in pytest 9.1, all higher-scoped fixtures (module, package, and session) defined as instance methods are now deprecated.

Removals and backward incompatible breaking changes

  • #14533: When using --doctest-modules, autouse fixtures with module, package or session scope that are defined inline in Python test modules (not plugins or conftests) will now possibly execute twice.

    If this is undesirable, move the fixture definition to a conftest.py file if possible.

    Technical explanation for those interested: When using –doctest-modules, pytest possibly collects Python modules twice, once as pytest.Module and once as a DoctestModule (depending on the configuration). Due to improvements in pytest’s fixture implementation, if e.g. the DoctestModule collects a fixture, it is now visible to it only, and not to the Module. This means that both need to register the fixtures independently.

    These iterables get exhausted after the first iteration, leading to tests getting unexpectedly skipped in cases such as running pytest.main() multiple times, using class-level parametrize decorators, or collecting tests multiple times.

    See parametrize-iterators for details and suggestions.

9.0.0 (2025-11-08)

pytest 9.0.0 (2025-11-05)

New features

  • #1367: Support for subtests has been added.

    subtests <subtests> are an alternative to parametrization, useful in situations where the parametrization values are not all known at collection time.

 for path in Path.cwd().glob("*.py"):
 with subtests.test(path=str(path)):
 assert contains_docstring(path)

    Each assert failure or error is caught by the context manager and reported individually, giving a clear picture of all files that are missing a docstring.

    In addition, unittest.TestCase.subTest is now also supported.

    This feature was originally implemented as a separate plugin in pytest-subtests, but since then has been merged into the core.

    [!NOTE] This feature is experimental and will likely evolve in future releases. By that we mean that we might change how subtests are reported on failure, but the functionality and how to use it are stable.

    While pytest, since version 6, supports configuration in pyproject.toml files under [tool.pytest.ini_options], it does so in an “INI compatibility mode”, where all configuration values are treated as strings or list of strings. Now, pytest supports the native TOML data model.

[pytest]
